companies.name: State Bank of India
companies.business: India’s largest bank by assets, spanning retail, corporate, treasury and international operations, with subsidiaries in insurance, asset management and cards.
thesis: Scale as a moat: the deposit franchise funds the book at a cost no peer can match, which shows up as a structurally wider net interest margin through the cycle.
Subsidiary value is not in the price: the insurance, asset management and card businesses are consolidated at cost rather than marked to their listed peers.
Credit costs have normalised: the corporate cycle that produced the 2018 losses has turned, and slippages are running below the through-cycle average.

theses.claim: Credit costs will remain structurally depressed.
theses.mechanism: Heavy provisioning in the past resulted in a PCR of 97.14%; recoveries from written-off TWO accounts now outpace fresh slippages.

theses.claim: Yield expansion via RAM mix shift.
theses.mechanism: The bank is actively rotating away from low-yielding corporate consortium loans toward high-yielding MSME and vehicle loans.
theses.evidence: Vehicle loans surged 35.1% YoY in FY26 while overall RAM grew 12.1%, taking RAM share above 55%.

theses.mechanism: Wage revision impacts (AS-15) have been fully absorbed in FY24/FY25; future headcount flatlines as digital transactions handle incremental volume.
theses.evidence: Operating expenses actually declined 2.5% YoY for the full year FY26.

companies.name: Bank of Baroda
companies.business: Public sector bank with a large domestic retail and MSME franchise and the widest international presence among Indian PSBs after the State Bank.
thesis: The international book is a genuine differentiator: overseas operations fund themselves and add fee income no domestic-only peer earns.
Retail mix has shifted decisively: home and vehicle loans now dominate incremental disbursement, lifting yields without adding unsecured risk.
Amalgamation is behind it: the Dena and Vijaya integration costs that suppressed three years of earnings have fully washed through.

theses.claim: Credit costs will remain structurally depressed.
theses.mechanism: Heavy provisioning in the past resulted in a PCR of 97.14%; recoveries from written-off TWO accounts now outpace fresh slippages.
theses.evidence: Credit cost fell to 0.08% in Q2FY25 and guided below 0.50% for FY26.

theses.claim: Yield expansion via RAM mix shift.
theses.mechanism: The bank is actively rotating away from low-yielding corporate consortium loans toward high-yielding MSME and vehicle loans.
theses.evidence: Vehicle loans surged 35.1% YoY in FY26 while overall RAM grew 12.1%, taking RAM share above 55%.

theses.mechanism: Wage revision impacts (AS-15) have been fully absorbed in FY24/FY25; future headcount flatlines as digital transactions handle incremental volume.
theses.evidence: Operating expenses actually declined 2.5% YoY for the full year FY26.

moat.evidence: Second largest PSB with 10,324 branches mobilizing Rs 17.11 Lakh Crore in deposits with 70.08% GoI backing.
moat.testSurvived: Survived the 2018 Nirav Modi fraud and subsequent massive NPA cycle without depositor flight.
moat.durability: Highly durable; sovereign backing ensures perpetual trust.

people.name: Atul Kumar Goel
people.background: Led the successful integration post-merger and the historic NPA cleanup.

people.name: Ashok Chandra
people.background: Currently driving the digital transition and profitability focus.

guidanceRecord.delivered: GNPA delivered at 5.73%, NIM delivered at 3.09% in H1.

capitalAllocation.summary: Capital historically eroded by massive NPA write-offs has been fully restored via government infusions and recent internal accruals, with surplus capital now funding organic growth without dilution.

mispricing.concern: The bank is a slow-moving PSU burdened by legacy bad loans and poor underwriting culture.
mispricing.answer: The balance sheet has been surgically cleansed (GNPA at 2.78%, Net NPA at 0.28%, PCR at 97%). Internal controls and e-surveillance are now fully automated, and RoA has crossed 1.0%—matching top-tier private banks.

peers.name: Bank of Baroda
peers.note: Closest comparable in size and business mix.

esg.social: Exceeded national goals for priority sector lending (41.1%) and weaker section credit.

esg.versusPeers: In line with major PSBs; trails private sector on granular ESG disclosures.

moat.evidence: Sovereign backing and second-largest PSB branch network of 10,324 drives sticky CASA deposits at 37%.

industryPosition.evidence: Systemically crucial as India's 3rd largest PSB with a 6.9% market share in total deposits.

revenueQuality.evidence: Core net interest income comprises ~70% of total income with yields on advances stable at 8.3%.

pricingPower.evidence: Passed on rate hikes effectively, maintaining global NIM at 2.99% despite peaking deposit costs.

customerQuality.evidence: RAM (Retail, Agri, MSME) segment accounts for over 55% of advances, reducing single-party corporate exposure.

productQuality.evidence: Standard banking products; digital adoption rising with PNB One active users at 250 Lakhs.

tamRunway.evidence: Indian credit growth continues at 12-15% annually, driven by a $3.5T economy expanding at 7% real GDP.

management.evidence: MD & CEO Atul Kumar Goel met FY24 guidance of reducing GNPA below 6% (delivered 5.73%) and RoA above 0.8%.

governance.evidence: Government holds 70.08%; previous severe frauds (2018) addressed by overhauling core banking and underwriting.

capitalAllocation.evidence: Raised equity to buffer losses and now self-funds growth, boasting a strong CRAR of 17.74% in FY26.

resilience.evidence: Absorbed massive legacy NPL shocks and COVID provisions, returning to record net profit of Rs 16,904 Cr in FY26.

tam.evidence: India's systemic credit market exceeds $2T, offering ample headroom for the 3rd largest state lender.

revenueRunway.evidence: Credit-Deposit ratio of 74% provides comfortable headroom to scale advances against a Rs 17.11 Lakh Cr deposit base.

epsGrowth.evidence: EPS grew from Rs 7.48 in FY24 to Rs 14.72 in FY26 on the back of sharp provision write-backs.

marketShare.evidence: Maintained 6.9% deposit share and ~6% advance share over three years without material dilution.

reinvestment.evidence: Retaining ~85% of record FY26 profits to organically fund 12% RAM advance growth.

incrementalReturns.evidence: RoA expanded from 0.46% in FY24 to 1.06% in FY26, signaling high incremental yield on assets.

operatingLeverage.evidence: Operating expenses declined 2.5% YoY in FY26 while operating profit grew 9.2% to Rs 29,290 Cr.

marginExpansion.evidence: NIMs largely peaked at ~3.0%, future PBT expansion driven by credit costs falling below 0.5%.

newProductsMarkets.evidence: PNB One Biz and digital lending journeys crossed Rs 17,500 Cr in origination in FY25.

exports.evidence: Global business is predominantly domestic, with overseas operations contributing less than 5% to profits.

capacity.evidence: Capital adequacy of 17.74% (Tier 1 at 15.15%) easily supports 3 years of 12-14% asset compounding.

execution.evidence: Successfully integrated OBC and UBI and brought GNPA down from 8.73% to 2.95% over two years.

longevity.evidence: Sovereign-owned universal bank central to India's financial system; high certainty of 15-year survival.

dcf.evidence: Base case cost of equity of 13% values the sustainable RoE of 14% at 1.2x P/B, upside of 25%.

relativeValuation.evidence: Trades at 0.95x FY26 Book Value vs SBI at 1.6x and Bank of Baroda at 1.2x despite similar RoA metrics.

peerValuation.evidence: Cheapest among the 'Big 3' PSBs on Price to Pre-Provision Operating Profit metric.

growthAdjustedValuation.evidence: PEG is meaningless for banks recovering from losses, but trades at <8x FY26 earnings.

scenarioAsymmetry.evidence: Upside to 1.5x P/B offers 50% gains, while sovereign backing and 97% PCR limit downside below 0.8x P/B.

catalystAdjusted.evidence: Expected provision write-backs over FY27 as recoveries from TWO accounts outpace fresh slippages.

balanceSheet.evidence: CRAR at 17.74% and PCR at 97.14% means the balance sheet is the strongest it has been in a decade.

accounting.evidence: Clean auditor reports post-2018 cleanup; provisions are now conservative with credit costs <0.5%.

governance.evidence: A technology outage in the mobile banking platform drew a regulatory direction to pause onboarding, since lifted. Controls have been remediated but the episode is recent enough to weigh.

promoter.evidence: Government of India holding remains robust at 70.08%, with zero pledges.

customerConcentration.evidence: Granular deposit base with top 20 depositors accounting for under 4% of total deposits.

regulatory.evidence: Compliant with RBI norms; ECL provisioning transition remains a manageable moderate risk for PSBs.

cyclicality.evidence: Banking is inherently leveraged to the macro-cycle; high rates suppress credit demand but aid margins.

competition.evidence: Faces intense competition from private banks on CASA mobilization, where gap is narrowing.

technology.evidence: Digital sourcing improved materially but core banking infrastructure still lags HDFC/ICICI benchmarks.

execution.evidence: Consistently lowered GNPA sequentially for 12 straight quarters, proving strong recovery execution.

liquidity.evidence: Massive trading liquidity with ADV >$30M ensures easy institutional entry and exit.

geopolitics.evidence: Over 95% of assets and liabilities are domestic, insulating from global trade disruptions.

valuationRisk.evidence: Trading at 1.0x book provides massive cushion; a de-rating to 0.8x is a shallow 20% drawdown.

dilution.evidence: Board reduced planned AT-1/Tier-2 capital raise due to strong internal accruals, limiting dilution risk.

financialQuality.evidence: Ten-year record marred by 2018-2020 losses, but last 3 years show high quality RoA expansion.

managementGovernance.evidence: Current management under MD Ashok Chandra is executing well, meeting public guidance conservatively.

technicalEntry.evidence: Stock is up ~5% on Q1FY27 results, establishing a clear breakout above the Rs 105 consolidation zone.

catalysts.evidence: Further rating upgrades from ICRA/CRISIL on sustained sub-3% GNPA are imminent.
